answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with slashing-backed answer deposits. (1) Every identity posting an answer locks a 50-POA deposit for one epoch, one per identity. (2) Peer graders flag duplicates and incoherent text; three independent flags send the answer to review at dawn of the round. (3) A confirmed fake burns the full deposit, while honest answers get it back. (4) Spinning up 1,000 fakes then costs 50,000 POA up front, most of it ash once they burn. The rule spreads like a trellis, holding each new agent to the same stake, and dishonest floods wash back out with the tide.
